citation.title: Recurrent Neural Networks for Multivariate Time Series with Missing Values
citation.authors: Z. Che, S. Purushotham, K. Cho, D. Sontag, Y. Liu

topic: GRU-D: recurrent model using masking and per-variable time-since-last-observation decays for irregularly observed multivariate series
own_question: Can missingness patterns (masks, time intervals) be built into a GRU to improve time series classification with informative missingness?
actual_method_and_evidence: Introduces trainable input decay toward the empirical mean and hidden-state decay as functions of per-variable time intervals, with masks fed to the gates. Evaluation used AUC from 5-fold CV on synthetic Gesture, PhysioNet 2012 and MIMIC-III clinical classification tasks, against mean, forward-fill and concatenation GRU baselines, two-step imputation and non-RNN models. GRU-D had the highest reported mean AUC in these tables. The tasks are classification, not regression nowcasting. There is no fusion-plasma data, and no real-time or latency evaluation.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Prior ML work on irregularly sampled series represents observation availability with masks and per-variable time-since-last-observation, and can decay stale values toward a default, motivating our use of strictly past CES report age as an input feature.
claim_checks.qualification: This is a concept from clinical classification. It is not validated for plasma CES nowcasting, and the authors give homeostasis as their rationale.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: In that clinical study, missingness indicators sometimes helped classification. The authors caution that when missingness is not informative, gains may be limited.
claim_checks.original_pdf_locator: Results Fig.4 discussion p.7; Limitations p.10
claim_checks.qualification: This is a dataset-specific author interpretation. Fig.4 was not visually checked.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Inputs are clinical measurements with masks and intervals, with targets being labels at end of a 48 h window. Early prediction used only past data. There is no CES or report-latency analogue.
validation_if_relevant: 5-fold CV on reused public datasets. Imputation baselines were tuned per the original codes. There is no untouched external test set.
forbidden_inferences: our estimator is novel relative to this or superior to it
reason_to_include_or_exclude: This is a canonical citation for representing stale or irregular observations via masks and time-since-last-report, which is relevant to anchoring on strictly past CES reports. Any temporal or causal framing of irregular inputs must come from our own paper. Cite only as methodological background; do not use it as plasma evidence or as a baseline we must implement.
